intent: I want a turf dog run at my Denver-area house. My HOA may say where the run goes and how big it can be, and it may want the run right against the house. What do Highlands Ranch, Sterling Ranch and Ken Caryl actually require, does turf count as the run's ground cover, how do I keep urine and rinse water off the swelling clay by my foundation, and how can I rinse the run under this winter's drought rules?
distinctValue: The national pet-turf page covers drainage and cleaning in general terms; the Grand Strand page is about heat, storm drains and flood permits; the northeast Florida page is general. This page answers a Denver-metro dog owner's placement question from written community rules: HRCA RIG 2.25 (a dog run must abut the house, rear or side yard, ground cover such as rock or mulch, 250 sq ft on most properties, one per property, chain link only if concealed) with 2.42.E (synthetic turf 2 ft from all property lines, sample and drainage plan); Sterling Ranch CAB's Controlled Pet Areas sheet (DRC approval, abutting the home behind yard fencing, not beside a corner sidewalk, street, common area or open space, plant screening, 200 sq ft or 25% of rear yard whichever is less, no chain link or electric dog fences); and Ken-Caryl's Dog Runs rule (fencing attached to perimeter fence or dwelling, site plan with dimensions) read together with its Firewise rule (no flammable materials such as mulch in the first 5 feet of a foundation). None of the three names turf for a dog run, so each becomes an 'ask the committee' step. Neither the Highlands Ranch, Sterling Ranch nor Ken Caryl town page covers these dog-run rules (the Ken Caryl page mentions the Firewise rule only for lawns). The drainage block states SP-14's rules (no ponding, sprinkler spray and downspout discharge 5 ft, gravel-and-fabric edging at least 5 ft 'can be used' to prevent percolation next to the foundation, runoff not toward a neighbor) and says plainly that SP-14 does not mention dogs or turf, so the rock-at-the-wall layout is a layout choice, not survey guidance; it addresses the conflict that a dog in a run abutting the house can use the rock strip and that a 5 ft strip is half of a 10 ft deep run, and points to HRCA's required drainage plan and Ken-Caryl's drainage section. Rinsing: Denver Water Resolution #002a-2026, quoted from the resolution itself (scope 'everyone who receives the Board's water', grass-watering ban, individual power-washing bar, hand-held hose with automatic shutoff nozzle for trees and shrubs, effective Oct 1, 2026 until further action of the Board), with Ken-Caryl Ranch Water as an example of a customer whose bill is not from Denver Water; and Thornton's 2026 turf rules published with its rebate (biodegradable cleaning products, odor maintenance), scoped to the rebate with an 'ask Thornton Water' step. Corrections from the second review: removed the claim that the resolution allows exceptions 'only under an approved water budget or variance' and the broad spray-system ban; removed 'Where Denver Water is on your bill'; removed the outdoor-rules page and its Stage 1 date range, and the drought page (its 'power washing only on your assigned watering day' line is superseded from Oct 1 by the resolution); removed the stitched SP-14 swales/fabric-lap paraphrase and the H2 that read as survey guidance for pet areas; removed the plastic-sheeting FAQ (repeats the winter article) and the generic 'turf by the foundation' FAQ; removed the generic city-rules block (Denver Sec. 8-73 and Thornton Sec. 6-34); removed the wins 'Waste and rinse water kept out of the street' and 'A dog run planned around your HOA's rules' and the visit promise to 'see where water leaves the yard'; added Ken-Caryl's Firewise rule and the Sterling Ranch sheet. Investigated but not used: Denver's household dog limit (denvergov.org refused connections on 2026-09-12, so no primary source could be opened) and PACFA rules 8 CCR 1201-11 for dog facilities (the current version could not be confirmed; ag.colorado.gov returned 403).

sources.label: HRCA: Residential Improvement Guidelines (adopted October 2024, updated June 2025)
supports: Cover and footer: "Adopted October 2024 | Updated June 2025". Server last-modified 8 July 2025; downloaded and read with pdftotext on 2026-09-12.
2.25. Dog Runs/Dog Houses. "ARC approval may be required. Dog Runs/Dog Houses must always be maintained, including timely cleanup/removal of dog waste and elimination of odors."

"A. Dog runs must: 1. Abut the house. 2. Be in the “rear” or “side” yard. 3. Have an appropriate ground cover (i.e.- rock, mulch, etc.). 4. Limited to a maximum of 250 square feet for most properties. 5. Limited to one (1) dog run per property. 6. Chain link enclosures may be approved, if “concealed” from view and do not extend above perimeter fencing."
2.41. Kennels. "Kennels are not allowed for commercial purposes. See Section 2.25. Dog Runs/Dog Houses." (Not used on the page.)

Definitions: "Dog Kennel: A structure where animals are individualized for purposes of boarding, breeding, or training or any type of commercial venture." "Dog Run: A contained space that is intended to allow one (1) or more animal's free movement in the outdoors." (Not used on the page.)

2.42.E. Artificial/Synthetic Turf. "ARC approval may be required. The submitted landscape plan will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis. A sample of the material and drainage plan is required along with the landscape plan." It must "Remain a minimum of two (2) feet from all property lines."
Section 2.25 does not mention artificial or synthetic turf as dog-run ground cover; the page's 'ask the ARC' step follows from that.

sources.label: Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board: Outdoor Controlled Pet Areas (DRC simple submittal one-sheet)
supports: Linked as "Controlled Pet Areas" under "DRC Simple Submittal One-Sheets" on https://sterlingranchcab.com/201/Design-Review-Documents (read 2026-09-12). The sheet shows no date.
"DRC approval is required for all outdoor controlled pet areas including dog runs and kennels."

"All outdoor controlled areas must be located in the side or rear yard, abutting the home and located behind yard fencing." "May not be located in a side yard adjacent to corner sidewalk, street, common area or open space."

"Must be substantially screened from view by fast-growing plant material. Evergreen plantings and grasses are required for four season screening." "Required to be kept in a clean, sanitary condition, and not allowed to fall into disrepair."

Dog Run: "May not exceed 200 square feet or more than 25% of the rear yard, whichever is less," "Constructed of fencing material matching that of lot-line fencing and stained to match lot-line fencing or may be black powder-coated steel" "Metal chain link enclosures are not permitted." "Pet mesh screen is required to be 2” x 4” galvanized welded wire mesh used on the inside of the fence, not to exceed the top rail in height, and continued down to ground level." "Covers (ex: tarps, sheets, blankets, etc.) are NOT allowed."

Kennel: "A free-standing panel-system kennel may not exceed 50 square feet and must be a maximum of 48 inches in height." Panels "painted to match the body color of the house, or black ornamental steel framed with wood that is painted to match the body color of the house". (Not used on the page.)
Invisible Fence Enclosures: "Electric dog fences are not allowed."
"The information on this sheet is NOT all inclusive of all Community Design Guidelines or Covenants." The sheet does not mention ground cover, surfacing or artificial turf.

sources.label: Ken-Caryl Ranch Master Association: property improvements (Dog Runs; Firewise; Drainage)
supports: Dog Runs: "Architectural Committee approval is required. Dog Runs shall be constructed as a privacy fence or transparent open rail fence. Dog run fencing must be attached to the perimeter fence or dwelling unit. Refer also to the fencing rules for your neighborhood."
Dog Runs submittal: "The chosen fencing style from the fencing rules for your neighborhood." "Site plan showing location of dog run with proposed dimensions" "Photo of the location"

Firewise – Mitigation and Safety: "Landscaping Near Foundations: No flammable materials, such as mulch, shall be placed within the first 5 feet of a home's foundation. Non-flammable alternatives such as rock, gravel, or hardscape features are encouraged." The rule does not mention artificial turf.

Drainage: "Section 3.09 of the Master Declaration requires that there be no interference with the established drainage pattern over any property. When installing landscaping, it is important to ensure that water drains away from the foundation of any house and that the flow patterns prevent water from flowing under, or ponding near or against the house foundation, walkways, sidewalks, and driveways of the primary and all adjacent properties. A resident may be required to provide an engineered drainage plan."
Read by curl and text extraction on 2026-09-12.

sources.label: Colorado Geological Survey Special Publication 14 (Jochim, first revision; 1981, revised fifth printing 1987): Home Landscaping and Maintenance on Swelling Soil
supports: Title page: "Colorado Geological Survey ... 1981 Revised, Fifth Printing, 1987"
"Water must not be allowed to pond near foundations or flatwork."
"(2) sprinkler systems should not spray any closer than 5 feet from the foundation."
"Water should be discharged no closer than 5 feet from the foundation." (splashblocks and downspouts)

"In fact an edging of gravel and geotextile fabric can be used very effectively around a house to prevent percolation of water into the soils next to the foundation. When used for this purpose, the edging should extend at least 5 feet out from the house."
"It is important that runoff be channeled away from the house, but at the same time not directed toward a neighbor's house or property."
SP-14 does not mention dogs, pet areas or artificial turf. The page says so and presents where the turf starts as a layout choice.

sources.label: Denver Water: Board Resolution #002a-2026 amending the Stage 1 drought declaration
supports: "Adopted and approved on August 26, 2026 by the City and County of Denver acting by and through its Board of Water Commissioners"

"a further drought response must be implemented requiring everyone who receives the Board’s water (inside and outside Denver, inside and outside the Combined Service Area, and lessees who receive nonpotable water and potable water under fixed-amount contracts) to reduce water use and participate in water conservation measures"
"Watering of all grass is prohibited after September 30, 2026, unless one of the following written exceptions apply."

"Trees, shrubs, and perennials may not be watered by spray irrigation but may continue to be watered any day by means of a hand-held hose with an automatic shutoff nozzle or low-volume non-spray irrigation."
"Power Washing by Individuals. Power washing may not occur except for immediate health or safety reasons."

"An irrigation system may be operated for installation, repair or reasonable maintenance, so long as the system is attended throughout the period of operation and water waste does not occur." (Not used on the page.)
"Board Resolution #002a-2026 becomes effective on October 1, 2026, through and until further action of the Board."
The resolution does not mention artificial turf, pets or dog areas; the page tells the reader to ask their water provider.

sources.label: Thornton Water: 2026 Artificial Turf Rules for Water-Wise Landscape Rebate (dated 1 January 2026)
supports: Title and footer: "2026 Artificial Turf Rules for Water-Wise Landscape Rebate", "1/1/2026".

General Maintenance: "General maintenance requirements are specified in Section 18-556 of the Thornton City Code. In addition, the following maintenance activities are required for artificial turf: 1. Cleaning, sanitizing, brushing, and removal of debris. Cleaning shall be done with biodegradable products."
"5. Regular maintenance to eliminate any odors, flat or matted areas, weeds, and looseness at edges, seams, or elsewhere."

The document is published for the rebate and does not say whether the maintenance list binds turf installed without it; the Municode chapter 18 content call returned only the chapter heading, so the page scopes the rule to the rebate and tells the reader to ask Thornton Water.
